findings.mechanism: Dirty sparse TSDF blocks invalidate their own cell-owner patch plus seven negative owner neighbours; positive topology and symmetric gradient halos preserve exact shared boundaries.
findings.interpretation: This layer already has a strong deterministic local-repair contract. Re-implementing 'incremental meshing' is not itself a new research contribution.

findings.mechanism: Reality Diff converts changed entity bounds into deterministic halo-expanded metric RegionKeys.
findings.interpretation: Useful substrate, but spatial dirty cells alone are not a minimal-work proof.

findings.mechanism: Dirty RegionKeys plus optional persistent ownership select splats for bounded local re-optimization while rejecting stable owned neighbours.
findings.computational_issue: selectGaussiansForLocalUpdate iterates over every Gaussian in the asset, computes a RegionKey, and probes the dirty-region hash table.
findings.complexity: O(N_gaussians) scan even when only a tiny fraction of the scene is dirty.
findings.interpretation: Semantic locality is present, but computational locality is not yet end-to-end.

findings.computational_issue: Current Metal sparse snapshot copies all resident blocks to the CPU before patch extraction.
findings.interpretation: A small world change may still cause global resident-state transfer even though meshing itself is local.

novelty_collisions: CL-Splats already performs local continual Gaussian optimization.
GaussianUpdate and GaME already perform continual/evolving-scene Gaussian updates.
EliGSiR already schedules continual RGB-D Gaussian mapping under bounded compute.
Recent Gaussian-triangulation work performs direct incremental scene reconstruction/mesh updates from geometric Gaussians.
Selective Gaussian editing/update is broadly occupied.
decision: KILL generic 'local update' as a headline claim. Continue only with dependency-certified heterogeneous minimal-work repair, where every layer exposes exact affected state and global-scan/global-copy leakage is measured explicitly.

next_probe.name: gaussian-region-index-v0
next_probe.goal: Measure whether a persistent RegionKey→Gaussian index eliminates O(N) selection scans while preserving exact selection semantics.
requiredMetrics: selection wall time when run on Apple silicon later
next_probe.killCondition: If indexing overhead or maintenance work removes the asymptotic/empirical advantage, or if exact selection semantics cannot be maintained, do not expand this mechanism.
